series: Walkthrough for the bank Short reorder-plan-2793-vs-1500.json, built Oct 7, 2026 for CMO review
hook: The reorder plan wants $2,793.90. Usable cash: $1,500
hook_say: This video shows what to do when your inventory reorder plan costs more than the cash you can spend, and how the planner decides what to buy first.

rows.label: Cash available for stock
rows.why: Start with the cash you can put into stock. The planner's sample shop has $1,800.

rows.label: Bills due before stock lands
rows.why: Then the bills that fall due before the new stock arrives. Here that is $300, and it comes off the top.

rows.label: Usable cash for this order
rows.why: That leaves $1,500 of usable cash. This is the real budget for the order, not the bank balance.

rows.label: Recommended order
rows.why: The plan looks at 16 products: what each one sells, 20% safety stock, and 14 days until the next order. To cover all of it, the plan wants $2,793.90.

rows.label: Shortfall
rows.why: That is $1,293.90 more than the usable cash, so the full plan cannot be bought today.

rows.label: Order now, most urgent first
rows.why: The Cash Check ranks every product by stockout risk and days of stock left. The canvas tote, with 7.5 days left, comes first and gets all 69 units. Down the list, it funds $1,497.50 now.

fix.label: Deferred to the next order
fix.why: The rest, $1,296.40, moves to the next order, with $2.50 of cash left over.
